notes: AUTONOMOUS REGION, not a separate hard-bordered nation nor a sphere overlay — treated the same tier as Myanmar's ethnic states on the mainland map, and author-confirmed 2026-09-26 to stay that way (a first-order-subdivision-respecting unit that's already drawn, per frameworks survey headline 7). Composition: Basilan, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Tawi-Tawi, plus the independent city of Cotabato — Sulu is explicitly EXCLUDED (final Philippine Supreme Court ruling, Nov 2024; formally executed by Executive Order No. 91, 30 July 2025) and stays part of Zamboanga Peninsula above. Over 89% Muslim (2024 census) — the country's most religiously distinct region by a wide margin. Population reconciled 2026-09-26: the frameworks survey's original 5.69 million (2024) figure was the pre-exclusion (with-Sulu) count; this row's 4,545,486 is the post-exclusion figure, and the ~1.1M gap is accounted for by Sulu's population moving to the Zamboanga Peninsula row above, confirmed via EO 91.

✅ SETTLED 2026-09-26: stays an ordinary Malaysian state, not promoted to Autonomous Zone status like Sarawak — its own secession-adjacent movement (e.g. STAR/Aspirasi) is real but less organized/documented than Sarawak's, and no party campaigned on secession in the 2025 Sabah state election. East Malaysia, joined the 1963 federation as a separate polity (former British North Borneo) under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), which promised broader autonomy and revenue share than delivered — both Sabah and Sarawak receive a 5% oil royalty (corrected 2026-09-26: an earlier note here said Sarawak received 20%; that figure is what both states have been demanding, not receiving — Sarawak's separate, genuine win was a 5% state sales tax on petroleum products), a live, current grievance (frameworks survey headline 8, §3.3), not merely historical. Also the object of a historic, unresolved Philippine claim rooted in the Sultanate of Brunei's 17th-century cession of the territory to Sulu (see the Zamboanga Peninsula row; direction corrected 2026-09-26).

⚠️ AUTHOR DECISION 2026-09-26: Sarawak gains Autonomous Zone status within Malaysia (the same designation as Aceh within the Indonesian core) — Malaysia itself stays intact as one sovereign country, this is a sub-country tier, not a new top-level bloc. Reasoning: Sarawak has the more organized, documented secession-adjacent movement of the two East Malaysian states (Parti Bumi Kenyalang campaigns explicitly for independence via referendum; the Sarawak For Sarawakians petition collected 270,000 signatures, over 10% of the state's population), though the secession-minded position is an explicit minority even within that movement, and no war forced this issue the way it did for Aceh — it's played out through elections and petitions. Former independent kingdom under the Brooke dynasty; joined 1963 under MA63 on the same disputed terms as Sabah. Both states receive a 5% oil royalty; Sarawak's separate win was a 5% state sales tax on petroleum products, not a higher royalty rate (corrected 2026-09-26; see the Sabah row and frameworks survey headline 8, §3.3).
